notes.title: [DEMO VERSION] Patch Release
notes.notes:
We have confirmed an issue in the Steam version where, on certain PC environments, the screen whites out and the game cannot proceed.
Today, Friday, September 12th at around 3:00 PM JST, we released a patch that resolves some of these issues.
If the issue persists, please try the following settings:

[list]
[*] Change your display refresh rate to 144Hz or lower in your Windows system settings
[*] Use a standard keyboard layout, not a custom one
[/list]
We will continue investigating other potential causes.
Thank you for your continued support of Digimon Story Time Stranger.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1984270/_/

notes.title: PAX West 2025: Digimon Story Time Stranger — So Many ‘Mons
notes.notes:
When Bandai Namco invited me to a four-hour preview for Digimon Story Time Stranger in the middle of PAX West 2025, I was intimidated to say the least. Powering through previews between PAX and gamescom 2025, I had gotten accustomed to rushed appointments, where I needed to get a grasp on all of the gameplay elements in a hurry. Luckily, Bandai Namco recognized that this approach would do a great disservice to Digimon Story Time Stranger, as even the lengthy preview wasn’t enough to truly take in all it has to offer.

In Digimon Story Time Stranger, you take on the role of an Operator who is able to journey between the human and digital worlds. In my preview, I was able to choose between a man and a woman, and whoever I didn’t choose was guiding me via my Digivice. You are sent to the Digital World to investigate a strange anomaly. If you’d like to learn more about the specifics of the Digimon Story Time Stranger story, you can see the story trailer below.

notes.title: Digimon Story: Time Stranger Preview — A Digital Adventure Rooted in Myth and Memory
notes.notes:
I used to love Digimon back when it first released. It was the game I played instead of Pokémon (I know, crazy), and it was the anime I loved to watch every Saturday morning. Needless to say, I was a fan of the franchise, although I’ve fallen off a bit in recent years. Still, when I had the chance to preview the latest installment, Digimon Story: Time Stranger, I was eager to see what was new.

Developed by Media Vision and published by Bandai Namco, this title is the newest entry in the Digimon Story series, marking a return almost eight years after Cyber Sleuth – Hacker’s Memory. For many, Time Stranger won’t be their first foray into the Digital World, yet the focus on story-driven progression and a vibrant monster-collecting system gives it an appropriate freshness for new fans while providing familiar satisfaction for veterans.

Players join the narrative as agents in a covert organization investigating incidents marked by digital anomalies and hazardous eruptions. The... Read more

notes.title: I don't believe it, but this Digimon RPG really was the best game I saw at SGF
notes.notes: For quite some time now I have been hearing rumors; scattershot whispers, in hushed tones. The Digimon Story games, they've been saying, are good. Subtitles like Cyber Sleuth would crop up in lists and recommendations from good friends, but I would always brush them off a bit. It's Digimon—surely nostalgia was the driving force of these rumors, I thought, and the RPGs behind them were only worth playing if you could identify MegaKabuterimon in a lineup... Read more.
